criteria.description: The #44 illegal-status shape is named and repairable, shown by named tests
criteria.note: Code covers isInvalidStatus (:325), the queue/scan lists (:702, :775), the doctor status-legal check (:1509-1522) and the --repair path (:1066-1088). Tests at :1013 (queue and scan name the entry, still counted open), :1048 (legal-log control), :1064 (doctor fails naming the file, passes on a legal log), :1093 (unreadable log), :1119 (repair works; mistyped literal writes nothing) and :1167 (legal literal or no guard exits 2). Lane: shared/resources/tests/*.test.mjs is in the npm test:suite glob (package.json), which .github/workflows/test.yml runs on every pull_request. I ran both suites on this head: 97/97 pass. QA report 1 names the tests in its table.

criteria.description: A parked entry returns to open, and no other status does, shown by named tests
criteria.note: The guard refuses `--status open` unless `--expect-status parked` or `--repair`. The test at :1203 covers parked to open with parked_until cleared, and the controls (actioned, open, no guard) each exit 2. Same per-PR lane as #1. See the advisory on the `--repair` carve-out.

criteria.description: review-cycle.md lists five decisions (grep in the QA report)
criteria.note: This is a documentation criterion, though a test pins it. Lines 99-103 list apply, decline, park, carry and propose a task. The test at :1001 asserts exactly those five bullets in order, plus the 'only on the user's yes' gate; :1024 pins the Step 7 scoped-review note. The skills/observe-work/tests/*.test.js glob is in npm test:suite, which runs per PR. I ran it: pass.

criteria.description: CI=true npm test wall time within 10% of develop, median of five alternating runs, uptime beside each
criteria.note: Bound: <=10% over develop. Command: five alternating `CI=true npm run test:remote -- --run test` runs per side on the LAN server, with `uptime` load averages recorded before each run. Measured on ee0e0a9e3, the PR code head, against origin/develop e092cf6eb. My median check from the table: develop 725, 725, 729, 809, 811 gives 729 s; head 724, 725, 737, 1201, 1296 gives 737 s. That is +1.1%, as the report states. The earlier commit M is named, and the run is 'measured on ee0e0a9e3, tree-equivalent to head': `finalise-delta.js docs-only --base ee0e0a9e3 --head HEAD --json` returned reason `tree-equivalent`, exit 0, with only the qa.3 report changed. The report does not hide the two high-load head runs; the median is not carried by them.

criteria.description: Each change has a mutation proof in the QA report
criteria.note: Units: isInvalidStatus; the scan-side list; the --repair legal-literal refusal; the --repair rejection on non-set-status commands; the enum check under --repair; the parked-only `open` guard; the doctor check; the SKILL.md status-legal row; the review-cycle fifth decision; and the scan-broken branch added in cycle 2. Each has a record naming the mutation and the test that went red: qa.1:107-115 covers the first nine, and qa.3:116 covers the scan-broken branch (mutated with `false && ...`, red on the named test, restored with `cmp` clean). I read each line. The two --repair guards share one test; the report says so and says each goes red for its own assertion.

criteria.description: bundle:check reports 0 problems; CI=true npm test passes
criteria.note: The bundle:check half I ran on this head: 'bundle freshness: 129 skill(s) checked, 0 problems', matching qa.3. The npm test half is a full-suite run. The committed evidence is qa.3: remote ci:fast exit 0 with 8601 tests, 8598 pass, 0 fail, on the tree the wall-time table measured. I ran the two changed suites here: 97/97 pass. The CI run on the PR head is not graded here; test.yml runs `npm test` on pull_request, and /finalise reads that state. If /finalise treats the npm test half as whole-CI-state, it should defer that half only.

criteria.description: observation-log.js doctor --json runs clean against the live log
criteria.note: Re-run on this head (HEAD 0d31a4f9b) with the workspace resolved through resolve-observation-workspace.sh: `doctor --json` returned reason ok, healthy true, exit 0, all five checks ok, with status-legal 'every status is legal'. A bare run without the workspace exits 2 `usage`; that is a lost shell variable, not a failure. The committed record is qa.1.md:56 (status-legal ok, invalidStatus empty). The per-PR test at :1064 pins the engine's clean-log behaviour. The live log itself is local state, not in the repo.

criteria.description: Existing --json consumers still parse the output; existing engine tests pass unchanged
criteria.note: The diff against origin/develop adds 254 lines to the engine test and 58 lines to the skill test. I counted 0 removed or modified lines in the engine test file, so no existing test was edited. The new fields are additive: invalidStatus on scan and queue, and a status-legal check. The pre-existing doctor reason and exit code are unchanged. qa.1.md:55 records the engine suite passing, and I ran both suites: 97/97. criteria-drift.js returned `clean` (exit 0).

advisories.note: The task's Target Architecture says `--status open` is accepted only with `--expect-status parked`, and any other use exits 2. The code at observation-log.js:1098 also accepts `--repair` with an illegal-literal guard (the header comment at :34 says so). Repairing a hand-edited illegal status straight to open is therefore possible. This is narrow, the guard still names the literal, and a test covers it. It is a small deviation from the prose 'no other status does'. The task and contract text should say it.
The doctor and test evidence above was run locally on HEAD 0d31a4f9b. The CI result on the PR head was not read by this agent.
